headline: Signal flat (0); 4 resolved trades still all losers (-44.1 bps) — sample far too thin to judge; BTC ~$66.0k
regime_note: Signal inactive (signal=0), BTC ~$65,990 essentially flat vs last check (~$65,955). No regime shift; live samples remain too small for any statistical conclusion.
assessment_md:
**How it's doing:** Nothing meaningful changed since last check. The strategy isn't currently signaling (signal=0), price is ~$65,990, roughly flat. The trade ledger still shows just **4 resolved trades**, all losers, averaging **-11.0 bps** each for **-44.1 bps total**.

**What the numbers tell us — and don't:** Four trades is far too few to conclude anything. A run of losers this small is well within normal noise for a signal whose expected edge is only ~4 bps gross. Losses ranged from -3.7 to -22.8 bps, i.e. a couple of unlucky larger misses dominate the tally. Separately, the broader 'window' stat counts 7 bets at 57% win and +1.2 bps net after a 3 bps cost — modestly positive but on an even flimsier basis. These two counters disagree simply because they're measuring tiny, different samples; neither is decisive.

**Context to keep in mind:** This was already flagged as a marginal signal — gross edge ~4 bps against a ~3.9 bps breakeven cost, so it is likely NOT net-profitable after realistic costs. The independent edge search still has **0 survivors** at the stricter 5 bps two-venue bar, reinforcing that any real edge is thin at best.

**Bottom line:** No alert. The all-losing ledger looks bad but is statistically meaningless at n=4. There is no guarantee of profit here — if anything, prior work suggests the edge may not clear costs. We need dozens of resolved trades before drawing conclusions. Keep watching; don't react to this noise.
